objects.reviewed_claim: For noncollinear finite planar P and t>0, the normalized lift (p_i,t z_c(i))/sqrt(1+t^2), with centered regular unit-edge simplex colors, has affine dimension at most two iff centered color columns lie in the centered source-plane span; exactly two used colors flatten iff their classes are distinct parallel level lines; exactly three used colors cannot flatten for n>=4. When the two-color condition and a proper contact coloring hold, a sufficiently small positive t preserves all pair lower bounds and strictly reduces the full-source diameter.

hypotheses_and_scope: P has n distinct points and affine span R^2, so rank(JP)=2, where J=I-11^T/n.
t>0; the simplex vertices used for distinct colours have pairwise distance one and are centered.
The three-colour rank statement assumes exactly three distinct simplex vertices are used; the two-colour characterization assumes exactly two nonempty classes.

The metric endpoint is conditional on a finite unit-separated source with diameter D>1, an actual proper contact colouring of every label (including isolates), and two colour classes lying on parallel lines so the prescribed lift is planarizable.
For the metric endpoint, choose t^2 below every same-colour noncontact slack d_ij^2-1; since the source is finite and the contact colouring is proper, each such slack is positive.

proof_reconstruction.rank_criterion: Let P be n×2 and Z be the n×(q-1) matrix of assigned simplex coordinates. The centered coordinate matrix of the normalized lift is (1/sqrt(1+t^2))[JP,tJZ]. The scalar factor does not change rank. Since rank(JP)=2 and t>0, rank([JP,tJZ])<=2 iff every column of JZ belongs to col(JP), equivalently JZ=JPA for some A. Removing centering gives Z=PA+1b^T, exactly an affine map on source points. Conversely that affine map gives the column inclusion and rank at most two.
proof_reconstruction.two_colours: With two distinct used simplex vertices, rank(JZ)=1, hence A in JZ=JPA has rank one because JP has full column rank. The associated affine map has parallel affine-line fibers, and the two color classes lie on distinct fibers. Conversely, two nonempty classes lying on distinct parallel lines are level sets of an affine scalar functional; an affine rescaling maps those two levels to the two simplex vertices. This includes a singleton class: its parallel fiber is distinct from the other class's line when the source is noncollinear.
proof_reconstruction.three_colours: Three used regular-simplex vertices are affinely independent, so rank(JZ)=2. Then rank(A)=2 and the associated affine map is injective. Each of the three color vertices has at most one source preimage, hence n<=3. At n=3 with all three colors used, the noncollinear source and the three simplex vertices each have centered span 1-perp in R^3, so the inclusion holds and the lift flattens. Thus for n>=4 this specified three-color lift cannot flatten.
proof_reconstruction.normalized_metric_endpoint: For a pair with source squared distance d^2, the normalized lifted squared distance is d^2/(1+t^2) for equal colors, and (d^2+t^2)/(1+t^2)=1+(d^2-1)/(1+t^2) for different colors. Properness puts every unit contact in different colors, where it remains exactly one. Different-color noncontacts stay strictly above one. Equal-color pairs are all noncontacts; choosing t^2<min_same(d^2-1) keeps them strictly above one. For all pairs d^2<=D^2, so new D'^2<= (D^2+t^2)/(1+t^2)<D^2 when D>1 and t>0. The rank result places the lifted labels in an affine plane; identifying that plane isometrically with R^2 preserves all computed distances.

unnormalized_rectangle.source: P={(0,0),(1,0),(0,2),(1,2)}, colors=(0,1,0,1), z_0=-1/2,z_1=1/2, t=1/2. The added color coordinate satisfies t z=x/2-1/4, so the unnormalized lift is already affine-flat of rank two.
unnormalized_rectangle.normalized_result: Source D^2=5 and same-color slack min=3. With t^2=1/4, the normalized pair squares are contacts 1, same-color vertical pairs 16/5, and cross-color diagonals 21/5. Thus minimum squared distance is 1 and D'^2=21/5<5.
unnormalized_rectangle.unnormalized_result: Equal-color distances stay unchanged; cross-color contacts change from squared distance 1 to 5/4 and diagonals from 5 to 21/4. Hence the unnormalized lift does not preserve contact lengths and increases the diameter; rank flattening alone cannot support the metric conclusion.
unnormalized_rectangle.result: Exact Fraction assertions pass; this is a countercontrol to the predecessor's unnormalized metric inference and a positive control for the corrected normalized endpoint.
